objects.description: Doubly linked list node used in the Linux kernel-style intrusive list API. Each user struct embeds a list_head member to link instances into a circular list. The head node typically points to itself when the list is empty.
Macro that yields the byte offset of MEMBER within TYPE. This is a macro definition, not a data type; ptr_type shown is the pointer form of its return type for completeness.
Linked-list node representing a source file in Kconfig parsing, tracking hierarchy (parent), name, and line number.
Three-valued logic used by Kconfig: no, module, yes.
Expression node types covering boolean/logical ops and comparisons for Kconfig expressions.
Variant payload for expression children: either a nested expression or a symbol reference.
AST node for Kconfig expressions. Binary nodes use left/right; E_SYMBOL stores symbol in left.sym; leaf/null can be used to represent constant yes.
Expression with its evaluated tristate value, used for dependencies and visibility tracking.
Holds a symbol's value (string/int/etc. via void*) paired with its tristate. Used for current and default values.
Domain/type of a configuration symbol.
Represents a Kconfig symbol (including choices). Tracks name, type, current and default values, visibility, flags, properties, and dependency relations.

objects.definition:
enum prop_type {
	P_UNKNOWN,
	P_PROMPT,	/* prompt "foo prompt" or "BAZ Value" */
	P_COMMENT,	/* text associated with a comment */
	P_MENU,	    /* prompt associated with a menu or menuconfig symbol */
	P_DEFAULT,	/* default y */
	P_CHOICE,	/* choice value */
	P_SELECT,	/* select BAR */
	P_IMPLY,	/* imply BAR */
	P_RANGE,	/* range 7..100 (for a symbol) */
	P_SYMBOL,	/* where a symbol is defined */
	P_RESET,	/* reset to defaults condition */
};
objects.description: Kinds of properties that can be attached to symbols/menu nodes (prompt, default, select, range, etc.).
Property node attached to symbols or menus capturing prompts, defaults, selects, ranges, and associated metadata and conditions.
Node in the Kconfig menu tree. Holds child/parent links, associated symbol (if any), prompt, visibility and dependency expressions, flags, help, and source location.
Helper struct for jump-list navigation in UIs: links to a target menu node and stores an offset; list_head for chaining.

Growable string buffer used by kconfig utilities. Tracks current length, owned char buffer, and an optional max line width for wrapping. Life-cycle helpers are declared in this header (str_new, str_free, str_append, str_printf, str_get).

Opaque menu node used by kconfig. Only forward-declared here; full definition is elsewhere. Accessed/manipulated via the menu_* API declared in this header. Details (fields, ownership, destruction) are unknown from this header.
Opaque file node used by kconfig’s internal file tracking. Only forward-declared via function return; no definition in this header. Constructed/retrieved via file_lookup; internal structure unknown.
Opaque symbol object representing a kconfig symbol. Only referenced here; defined elsewhere (likely in expr.h). Managed via sym_* and related APIs. Details unknown in this header.

Opaque property descriptor attached to menu entries/symbols in kconfig. Only referenced here; definition is elsewhere. Created/returned by menu_add_prop, menu_add_prompt, menu_add_expr, menu_add_symbol, sym_get_range_prop, prop_get_symbol.
Opaque/incomplete list node type (Linux kernel list). Only referenced as a parameter; definition not present in this header.

External array-of-C-strings type as used by the declared image resources (e.g., xpm_load, xpm_save). However, this header only declares variables of this type and does not define any new custom types (no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes). This entry is included only to note that there are no custom type definitions present; the underlying type is a built-in pointer-to-pointer of const char and not a custom alias.

functions.name: list_empty
functions.signature: static inline int list_empty(const struct list_head *head)
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the doubly-linked list identified by head is empty. Intended for circular Linux-style list_head lists where head points to the sentinel node whose next/prev point back to itself when empty.
requirements: head must be a valid, initialized list head (created via LIST_HEAD or initialized to LIST_HEAD_INIT).
head must not be NULL.
The list structure must be well-formed (head->next and head->prev are valid pointers within the list).
Return value is nonzero when empty, zero otherwise.

functions.name: __list_add
functions.signature: static inline void __list_add(struct list_head *_new, struct list_head *prev, struct list_head *next)
functions.description: Internal primitive to insert the node _new between two known consecutive nodes prev and next in a doubly-linked, circular list. Used by higher-level add helpers.
requirements: prev and next must be consecutive nodes in the same list (i.e., prev->next == next and next->prev == prev) before the call.
_new, prev, and next must be non-NULL.
_new must be in a state where its next/prev can be set (not required to be part of any list).
The caller must ensure list integrity; this function does no validation.
Only use for internal list manipulation when the correct prev/next are already known, as noted in the comment.

functions.name: list_add_tail
functions.signature: static inline void list_add_tail(struct list_head *_new, struct list_head *head)
functions.description: Inserts _new at the tail of the list whose sentinel is head (i.e., just before head). Useful for implementing FIFO queues using a circular list_head list.
requirements: head must be a valid, initialized list head for a circular list (e.g., created with LIST_HEAD or initialized with LIST_HEAD_INIT).
_new must be non-NULL.
_new should not currently be linked into any list (its next/prev will be overwritten).
The list headed by head must be well-formed prior to insertion.

functions.name: __list_del
functions.signature: static inline void __list_del(struct list_head *prev, struct list_head *next)
functions.description: Internal primitive to unlink the node between prev and next by relinking prev->next to next and next->prev to prev. Used by higher-level deletion helpers.
requirements: prev and next must be consecutive nodes in the same list (i.e., prev->next == node_to_remove and node_to_remove->next == next prior to removal; equivalently, they must border the element being removed).
prev and next must be non-NULL.
Caller is responsible for having identified the correct neighboring nodes and for maintaining list integrity; no validation is performed.
Only use for internal list manipulation where the correct prev/next are already known, as noted in the comment.

functions.name: list_del
functions.description: Removes entry from its current doubly-linked list by splicing its neighbors together, then poisons entry->next and entry->prev to catch use-after-delete. After this call, entry is in an undefined state and not considered an empty standalone list node.
requirements: entry must be non-NULL.
entry must currently be linked into a valid, well-formed list (entry->prev and entry->next must be valid and mutually consistent).
After deletion, entry->next and entry->prev are set to poison values; do not dereference or reuse them without reinitialization.
Do not assume list_empty(entry) will be true after deletion; entry is not a list head and is left in an undefined state, per the note in the comment.

functions.name: lookup_file
functions.description: Finds and returns the file node corresponding to the given file name within the internal file list used by the Kconfig parser.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated string
Returns NULL if no matching file is found; callers must handle a NULL return

functions.name: expr_alloc_symbol
functions.description: Allocates and returns an expression node representing a symbol reference in the Kconfig expression tree.
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a struct symbol

functions.name: expr_alloc_one
functions.signature: struct expr *expr_alloc_one(enum expr_type type, struct expr *ce);
functions.description: Allocates a unary expression node of the specified type with a single child expression (ce). Typical unary use is E_NOT or wrapping a single subexpression.
requirements: type must be a valid enum expr_type value appropriate for a unary expression (e.g., E_NOT)
ce must be a valid expression pointer when required by the given type

functions.name: expr_alloc_two
functions.signature: struct expr *expr_alloc_two(enum expr_type type, struct expr *e1, struct expr *e2);
functions.description: Allocates a binary expression node of the specified type with left/right child expressions e1 and e2 (e.g., E_AND, E_OR, comparisons).
requirements: type must be a valid enum expr_type value appropriate for a binary expression (e.g., E_AND, E_OR, E_EQUAL, etc.)
e1 and e2 must be valid expression pointers when required by the given type

functions.name: expr_alloc_comp
functions.signature: struct expr *expr_alloc_comp(enum expr_type type, struct symbol *s1, struct symbol *s2);
functions.description: Allocates a comparison expression node comparing two symbols, using the specified comparison operator.
requirements: type must be one of the comparison types: E_EQUAL, E_UNEQUAL, E_LTH, E_LEQ, E_GTH, or E_GEQ
s1 and s2 must be valid pointers to struct symbol

functions.name: expr_alloc_and
functions.description: Convenience allocator that creates a logical AND (E_AND) expression node from two child expressions.
requirements: e1 and e2 must be valid expression pointers

functions.name: expr_alloc_or
functions.description: Convenience allocator that creates a logical OR (E_OR) expression node from two child expressions.
requirements: e1 and e2 must be valid expression pointers

functions.name: expr_copy
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of the given expression tree.
requirements: org must be a valid pointer to an expression; returns NULL if org is NULL (behavior not specified in header; callers should handle a possible NULL result)

functions.name: expr_free
functions.description: Frees an expression tree previously allocated by the expr_alloc_* family or expr_copy.
requirements: e may be NULL (common free semantics; behavior not specified in header)
The expression tree must not be used after being freed

functions.name: expr_eliminate_eq
functions.description: Performs algebraic simplification by eliminating equalities between two expressions in place, potentially modifying or replacing the pointed-to expressions.
requirements: ep1 and ep2 must be non-NULL pointers to expression pointers
*ep1 and *ep2, if non-NULL, must point to valid expression trees

functions.name: expr_eq
functions.description: Tests structural/logical equality of two expressions; returns nonzero if equivalent, zero otherwise.
requirements: e1 and e2 must be valid expression pointers or NULL; callers must interpret the return value as boolean

functions.name: expr_calc_value
functions.description: Evaluates an expression to a tristate value (n, m, y) based on current symbol values and dependencies.
requirements: e must be a valid expression pointer or NULL (NULL may be treated as 'y' in some helpers; exact behavior not specified)
Callers must interpret the returned tristate according to enum tristate

functions.name: expr_trans_bool
functions.description: Transforms/simplifies an expression to its boolean form, folding tristate semantics into boolean logic where applicable.
requirements: e must be a valid expression pointer or NULL

functions.name: expr_eliminate_dups
functions.description: Removes duplicate terms from an expression tree and returns the simplified expression (which may be the same pointer or a new tree).
requirements: e must be a valid expression pointer or NULL
Caller must use the returned pointer as the current expression (original may be freed or reused internally)

functions.name: expr_transform
functions.description: Applies general transformation/simplification rules to an expression tree and returns the transformed expression.
requirements: e must be a valid expression pointer or NULL
Caller must use the returned pointer as the updated expression

functions.name: expr_contains_symbol
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the given expression references the specified symbol anywhere in the tree, zero otherwise.
requirements: dep must be a valid expression pointer or NULL
sym must be a valid pointer to struct symbol

functions.name: expr_depends_symbol
functions.description: Determines whether the given expression has a dependency on the specified symbol (stronger than simple containment), returning true or false.
requirements: dep must be a valid expression pointer or NULL
sym must be a valid pointer to struct symbol

functions.name: expr_trans_compare
functions.signature: struct expr *expr_trans_compare(struct expr *e, enum expr_type type, struct symbol *sym);
functions.description: Transforms an expression by comparing it to the given symbol using the specified comparison operator; returns a new/updated expression.
requirements: type must be a comparison operator type (E_EQUAL, E_UNEQUAL, E_LTH, E_LEQ, E_GTH, or E_GEQ)
e must be a valid expression pointer or NULL
sym must be a valid pointer to struct symbol

functions.name: expr_fprint
functions.description: Prints a textual representation of the expression to the given FILE stream (for debugging or diagnostics).
requirements: out must be a valid, open FILE* for writing
e may be NULL; output in that case is implementation-defined

functions.name: expr_gstr_print
functions.description: Appends a textual representation of the expression to the given gstr string builder.
requirements: gs must be a valid pointer to a gstr buffer/object
e may be NULL; resulting output is implementation-defined

functions.name: expr_gstr_print_revdep
functions.signature: void expr_gstr_print_revdep(struct expr *e, struct gstr *gs, tristate pr_type, const char *title);
functions.description: Appends a textual representation of reverse dependencies derived from the expression into gs, using the given priority/type and title for formatting.
requirements: gs must be a valid pointer to a gstr buffer/object
title must be a valid, null-terminated string or NULL if supported (not specified)
pr_type must be a valid enum tristate value
e may be NULL; resulting output is implementation-defined

functions.name: expr_is_yes
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the expression is logically 'yes' (true). Treats NULL as 'yes' and also matches an E_SYMBOL node equal to symbol_yes.
requirements: e may be NULL; in that case the function returns true (nonzero)
If non-NULL, e->type must be E_SYMBOL and e->left.sym comparable to &symbol_yes to be considered 'yes'

functions.name: expr_is_no
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the expression is logically 'no' (false). Matches an E_SYMBOL node equal to symbol_no. NULL is treated as not 'no' (returns 0).
requirements: If e is non-NULL, e->type must be E_SYMBOL and e->left.sym comparable to &symbol_no to be considered 'no'
e may be NULL; in that case the function returns 0

functions.name: CONFIG_prefix
functions.description: Returns the effective CONFIG_ prefix string to use for configuration symbols. It checks the environment variable named "CONFIG_" and, if set, returns its value; otherwise returns the built-in default prefix string. Intended for code that needs the current CONFIG prefix at runtime.
requirements: No arguments; may call getenv internally, which is process-global and not thread-safe on some platforms.
The returned pointer is valid as long as the environment or static storage remains unchanged.

functions.name: zconfdump
functions.description: Dumps the current Kconfig state/configuration to the given output stream. Used for diagnostics or emitting configuration data.
requirements: out must be a valid, open FILE* for writing.
Called after the configuration state has been initialized/loaded.

functions.name: zconf_starthelp
functions.description: Begins a help text section during Kconfig parsing. Typically called by the parser when encountering a help block.
requirements: Must be called in the correct parser state (during configuration file parsing).

functions.name: zconf_fopen
functions.description: Opens a configuration-related file by name and returns a FILE* stream. May search along Kconfig include paths.
requirements: name must be a non-null, null-terminated file name.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to handle open failures.
The returned FILE* must be closed by the caller with fclose().

functions.name: zconf_initscan
functions.description: Initializes the Kconfig lexer/scanner for the specified file.
requirements: name must be a non-null path to a readable Kconfig file.
Must be called before zconf_nextfile() and before invoking the lexer (e.g., yylex()).

functions.name: zconf_nextfile
functions.description: Pushes or switches the Kconfig scanner to the next file (e.g., upon encountering 'source' directives).
requirements: name must be a non-null, readable file path.
Must be called after zconf_initscan() has initialized the scanner.

functions.name: zconf_lineno
functions.description: Returns the current line number within the file being scanned by the Kconfig lexer.
requirements: Must be called after scanner initialization (zconf_initscan()).

functions.name: zconf_curname
functions.description: Returns the name/path of the file currently being scanned by the Kconfig parser.
requirements: Must be called after scanner initialization (zconf_initscan()).
The returned pointer remains valid while the underlying filename storage is valid (implementation-defined).

functions.name: conf_get_configname
functions.description: Returns the path/name of the active .config file used by Kconfig.
requirements: Call after configuration system initialization.
Caller should not modify the returned string.

functions.name: set_all_choice_values
functions.description: For a choice symbol, sets all choice values according to defaults or selection rules. Used during configuration resolution.
requirements: csym must be a non-null pointer to a choice-type symbol.

functions.name: xfwrite
functions.signature: static inline void xfwrite(const void *str, size_t len, size_t count, FILE *out);
functions.description: Wrapper around fwrite that asserts len != 0 and prints an error to stderr if fwrite does not write the requested number of items. Does not return an error code.
requirements: len must be non-zero (enforced by assert).
out must be a valid, open FILE* for writing.
If count > 0, str must point to at least len*count readable bytes.
Caller must handle the fact that errors are only reported via stderr; no exception or return code is provided.

functions.name: file_lookup
functions.description: Looks up or loads a file structure corresponding to the given name within the Kconfig internal file tracking.
requirements: name must be a non-null, null-terminated file name/path.
Caller must handle a NULL return if the file is not found/created (behavior is implementation-defined).

functions.name: xmalloc
functions.description: Allocates size bytes of memory. By convention for x* allocators, this likely never returns NULL on failure (may abort), but exact behavior is implementation-defined here.
requirements: size is the number of bytes to allocate; behavior for size==0 is implementation-defined.
Caller owns the returned buffer and must free it with free() unless otherwise documented.

functions.name: xcalloc
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized memory for an array of nmemb elements of size bytes each. Typical x* behavior is to avoid returning NULL on failure (may abort), but exact behavior is not specified here.
requirements: nmemb and size specify the total allocation; behavior on overflow or zero sizes is implementation-defined.
Caller owns the returned buffer and must free it with free().

functions.name: xrealloc
functions.description: Changes the size of the memory block pointed to by p to size bytes, returning a pointer to the new memory. Likely aborts on failure in x* style, but exact behavior is not specified.
requirements: p may be NULL to behave like allocation; otherwise must be a pointer obtained from malloc-family functions.
Caller must manage the returned pointer and free it with free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: xstrdup
functions.description: Duplicates the string s and returns a newly allocated copy. Likely never returns NULL in x* style, but exact failure behavior is not specified.
requirements: s must be a non-null, null-terminated string.
Caller must free the returned string with free().

functions.name: xstrndup
functions.description: Duplicates at most n bytes from string s, returning a newly allocated, null-terminated copy.
requirements: s must be a non-null, null-terminated string (or at least n readable bytes).
Caller must free the returned string with free().

functions.name: yylex
functions.description: The lexer function generated by flex/lex for Kconfig. Returns the next token as an integer code.
requirements: Must be called after the scanner has been initialized (zconf_initscan()).
Caller must handle end-of-input and token values according to the grammar.

functions.name: str_new
functions.description: Creates and returns a new gstr string builder instance with default state.
requirements: Use with the companion functions (str_append, str_printf, str_get, str_free).
The returned struct should be treated as initialized and later passed to str_free() to release resources.

functions.name: str_free
functions.description: Frees resources held by a gstr string builder.
requirements: gs must be non-null and previously initialized by str_new().
After calling, gs should not be used unless reinitialized.

functions.name: str_append
functions.description: Appends the string s to the gstr builder, optionally wrapping lines based on max_width.
requirements: gs must be non-null and initialized by str_new().
s must be a non-null, null-terminated string.

functions.name: str_printf
functions.description: Appends formatted text to the gstr builder using printf-style formatting.
requirements: gs must be non-null and initialized by str_new().
fmt must be a non-null format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt.

functions.name: str_get
functions.description: Returns a C string built so far from the gstr builder. Ownership and lifetime semantics are implementation-defined here (may return internal buffer).
requirements: gs must be non-null and initialized by str_new().
Caller must follow the implementation’s ownership rules for the returned pointer (unknown from this header).

functions.name: _menu_init
functions.description: Initializes the menu system used by Kconfig.
requirements: Must be called before other menu manipulation/query functions.

functions.name: menu_warn
functions.description: Emits a warning message associated with a specific menu node, using printf-style formatting.
requirements: menu should be a valid pointer to a menu node (may be NULL if allowed by implementation).
fmt must be a non-null format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt.

functions.name: menu_add_menu
functions.description: Begins a new submenu/menu node and returns it.
requirements: Must be called within a valid menu construction context (after _menu_init()).
Caller must use the returned menu in subsequent menu operations.

functions.name: menu_end_menu
functions.description: Ends the current submenu/menu block.
requirements: Must match a preceding menu_add_menu() call and be used within a valid construction context.

functions.name: menu_add_entry
functions.description: Adds a menu entry associated with the given symbol.
requirements: sym must be a non-null pointer to a valid symbol.
Must be called within an active menu construction context.

functions.name: menu_add_dep
functions.description: Adds a dependency expression to the current menu entry or property.
requirements: dep must be a non-null pointer to a valid expression.
Must be called while a target entry/property is active.

functions.name: menu_add_visibility
functions.description: Adds a visibility condition expression to the current menu entry.
requirements: dep must be a non-null pointer to a valid expression.
Must be called while a target menu entry is active.

functions.name: menu_add_prop
functions.signature: struct property *menu_add_prop(enum prop_type type, struct expr *expr, struct expr *dep);
functions.description: Adds a property of the specified type to the current menu context, with an optional value expression and dependency.
requirements: type must be a valid enum prop_type value.
expr may be NULL or a valid expression depending on property type (implementation-defined).
dep may be NULL or a valid dependency expression.
Must be called within an active menu context.

functions.name: menu_add_prompt
functions.signature: struct property *menu_add_prompt(enum prop_type type, char *prompt, struct expr *dep);
functions.description: Adds a prompt (or similar text property) with a given type, prompt string, and optional dependency.
requirements: type must be a valid enum prop_type value.
prompt must be a non-null, null-terminated string.
dep may be NULL or a valid expression.
Must be called within an active menu context.

functions.name: menu_add_expr
functions.signature: void menu_add_expr(enum prop_type type, struct expr *expr, struct expr *dep);
functions.description: Adds a property represented by an expression with an optional dependency to the current menu context.
requirements: type must be a valid enum prop_type value.
expr must be a valid expression pointer (may be NULL depending on type; implementation-defined).
dep may be NULL or a valid dependency expression.
Must be called within an active menu context.

functions.name: menu_add_symbol
functions.signature: void menu_add_symbol(enum prop_type type, struct symbol *sym, struct expr *dep);
functions.description: Adds a property referencing a symbol with an optional dependency to the current menu context.
requirements: type must be a valid enum prop_type value.
sym must be a non-null pointer to a valid symbol.
dep may be NULL or a valid dependency expression.
Must be called within an active menu context.

functions.name: menu_finalize
functions.description: Finalizes the menu tree under the specified parent, resolving properties and dependencies.
requirements: parent must be a valid pointer to a menu node that acts as the root of the subtree to finalize.
Should be called after menu construction is complete.

functions.name: menu_set_type
functions.description: Sets the type of the current menu symbol (e.g., bool, tristate, string). Exact mapping is implementation-defined.
requirements: type must be a valid symbol type constant for this Kconfig implementation.
Must be called when a current symbol context is active.

functions.name: menu_is_empty
functions.description: Returns true if the given menu node has no visible/active entries.
requirements: menu must be a non-null pointer to a valid menu node.

functions.name: menu_is_visible
functions.description: Returns true if the given menu node is visible under current conditions (dependencies, visibility).
requirements: menu must be a non-null pointer to a valid menu node.

functions.name: menu_has_prompt
functions.description: Returns true if the given menu node has a prompt text defined.
requirements: menu must be a non-null pointer to a valid menu node.

functions.name: menu_get_prompt
functions.description: Returns the prompt string for the given menu node, if any.
requirements: menu must be a non-null pointer to a valid menu node.
Caller should treat the returned pointer as read-only and implementation-managed.

functions.name: menu_get_parent_menu
functions.description: Returns the parent menu of the given menu node.
requirements: menu must be a non-null pointer to a valid menu node.

functions.name: menu_has_help
functions.description: Returns true if the given menu node has help text associated with it.
requirements: menu must be a non-null pointer to a valid menu node.

functions.name: menu_get_help
functions.description: Returns the help text for the given menu node, if available.
requirements: menu must be a non-null pointer to a valid menu node.
Caller should treat the returned pointer as read-only and implementation-managed.

functions.name: get_jump_key_char
functions.description: Returns the character code used as the jump key in menu navigation (UI helper).
requirements: No arguments; return value meaning is defined by the UI layer.

functions.name: get_relations_str
functions.signature: struct gstr get_relations_str(struct symbol **sym_arr, struct list_head *head);
functions.description: Builds and returns a gstr containing relationships (e.g., dependencies, selects) among symbols and/or items in the provided list.
requirements: sym_arr must be a valid pointer to an array of symbol pointers (may be NULL depending on usage; implementation-defined).
head must be a non-null pointer to a valid list_head describing relations.
Returned gstr must be released with str_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: menu_get_ext_help
functions.description: Appends extended help information for the given menu node into the provided gstr buffer.
requirements: menu must be a non-null pointer to a valid menu node.
help must be a non-null, initialized gstr (from str_new()).

functions.name: sym_clear_all_valid
functions.description: Clears validity/dirty flags on all symbols, forcing recomputation of values/dependencies as needed.
requirements: Should be called when the symbol graph needs re-evaluation (no arguments).

functions.name: sym_choice_default
functions.description: Returns the default selected symbol for a given choice-type symbol.
requirements: sym must be a non-null pointer to a choice symbol.

functions.name: sym_get_range_prop
functions.description: Returns the range property (min/max) associated with the given symbol, if any.
requirements: sym must be a non-null pointer to a symbol.

functions.name: sym_get_string_default
functions.description: Returns the default string value for the given symbol, if defined.
requirements: sym must be a non-null pointer to a symbol.
Returned pointer should be treated as read-only and implementation-managed.

functions.name: sym_check_deps
functions.description: Checks the dependencies of the given symbol and returns a related symbol indicating a dependency issue, or possibly the same symbol if OK (exact semantics implementation-defined).
requirements: sym must be a non-null pointer to a symbol.

functions.name: prop_get_symbol
functions.description: Returns the symbol referenced by the given property, if applicable.
requirements: prop must be a non-null pointer to a property object.

functions.name: sym_get_tristate_value
functions.description: Returns the current tristate value of the symbol (n/m/y).
requirements: sym must be a non-null pointer to an initialized symbol with a valid curr.tri field.

functions.name: sym_get_choice_value
functions.description: For a choice symbol, returns the currently selected symbol value.
requirements: sym must be a non-null pointer to a symbol.
sym must represent a choice whose current value is a symbol pointer (implementation-defined).

functions.name: sym_is_choice
functions.description: Returns true if the symbol is a choice (SYMBOL_CHOICE flag set).
requirements: sym must be a non-null pointer to a symbol.

functions.name: sym_is_choice_value
functions.description: Returns true if the symbol is a value within a choice (SYMBOL_CHOICEVAL flag set).
requirements: sym must be a non-null pointer to a symbol.

functions.name: sym_is_optional
functions.description: Returns true if the symbol is marked optional (SYMBOL_OPTIONAL flag set).
requirements: sym must be a non-null pointer to a symbol.

functions.name: sym_has_value
functions.description: Returns true if the symbol currently has a user-defined value (SYMBOL_DEF_USER flag set).
requirements: sym must be a non-null pointer to a symbol.

__list_add
list_add_tail
__list_del

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filename for writable file
# Requirements inferred from stubs:
# - Must be a valid path that can be opened for writing with fopen(..., "wb" or "wb+")
# - Should avoid exceeding OS path length limits
# - Should sometimes include directories, sometimes just a filename
# - Should avoid characters that are invalid on common platforms
# - Should be unique-ish per call to avoid collisions
# - No I/O side effects here; just generate the path string bytes
# - Result must be bytes for the fuzzer input buffer

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.,@#%+="

# Some interesting directory components to exercise path handling
DIR_TOKENS = [
    "tmp", "var", "log", "config", "kconf", "build", "out",
    ".", "..", "..hidden", ".cache", "subdir", "data",
]

EXTENSIONS = [
    ".bin", ".dat", ".out", ".tmp", ".cfg", ".kconf", ".txt", ""
]

PREFIXES = [
    "/tmp/", "/var/tmp/", "/dev/shm/", "./", "../", ""  # Prefer writable/common
]

def _rand_token(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    ln = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure first char not a dot unless explicitly chosen via DIR_TOKENS
    first_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
    s = rng.choice(first_chars)
    if ln > 1:
        s += ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(ln - 1))
    return s

def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand_token(rng, 3, 20)
    # Occasionally add multiple tokens joined by dashes to create longer names
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        parts = [base]
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            parts.append(_rand_token(rng, 2, 10))
        base = '-'.join(parts)
    ext = rng.choice(EXTENSIONS)
    return base + ext

def _rand_dirpath(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create 0..3 directory components, with a bias toward 1..2
    depth = rng.choices([0,1,2,3], weights=[2,4,3,1], k=1)[0]
    comps: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            comps.append(rng.choice(DIR_TOKENS))
        else:
            comps.append(_rand_token(rng, 2, 12))
    return '/'.join(comps) + ('/' if comps else '')

def _sanitize_path(path: str) -> str:
    # Avoid trailing spaces or dots which can be problematic on some filesystems
    path = path.strip()
    # Collapse multiple slashes
    while '//' in path:
        path = path.replace('//', '/')
    # Avoid path length too large
    return path[:240]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a prefix favoring writable or relative directories
    prefix = rng.choice(PREFIXES)

    # Optionally add nested directories after the prefix
    dirpath = _rand_dirpath(rng)

    fname = _rand_filename(rng)

    # Occasionally embed a numeric seed or timestamp-like pattern to increase uniqueness
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        suffix_num = rng.randrange(0, 1_000_000)
        fname = f"{fname}.{suffix_num}"

    # Build the path
    path = f"{prefix}{dirpath}{fname}"

    # Ensure path is not empty and not a directory
    if path.endswith('/'):
        path += _rand_filename(rng)

    # Final sanitation
    path = _sanitize_path(path)

    # Ensure minimal length
    if not path:
        path = "./out.bin"

    # Return as bytes (UTF-8)
    return path.encode('utf-8')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary string
# Used by stubs for: titles, prompts, messages, symbol names, general strings, and filenames.
# Goal: produce a bytes buffer that, when consumed by the fuzzer as a string or file content,
# yields valid, interesting C strings. We include a small corpus of Kconfig-like tokens,
# varying lengths, ASCII ranges, UTF-8, and edge-case constructs. The buffer should be <= 4096 bytes.

# We construct a concatenation of multiple null-terminated strings to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR provider
# with a pool of different strings in one buffer. Many fuzzing frameworks split or pick substrings
# from the initial buffer. Keeping multiple NUL-terminated entries increases variety while ensuring
# each entry is a valid C string.

# We also include sections that look like filenames and simple Kconfig snippets to drive code paths
# that depend on recognizable content.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

_DEF_STRINGS = [
    # Short edge cases
    "",  # empty string
    " ",
    "\t",
    "0",
    "1",
    "yes",
    "no",
    "mod",
    "y",
    "n",
    "m",
    # Typical identifiers and prompts
    "CONFIG_FOO",
    "CONFIG_BAR",
    "FOO",
    "BAR",
    "Enable feature X",
    "Disable feature Y?",
    "Select driver Z",
    # Filenames / paths
    "Kconfig",
    "arch/x86/Kconfig",
    "drivers/net/Kconfig",
    "include/config/auto.conf",
    "../relative/path.cfg",
    "/absolute/path/to/Kconfig",
    # Formats for printf
    "value=%d",
    "%s %d",
    "%p %x",
    # Unicode prompts (valid UTF-8)
    "München",
    "配置オプション",
    "опция",
    "选项: 启用",
    # Comparison operators and expression tokens
    "&&",
    "||",
    "==",
    "!=",
    "<=",
    ">=",
    "<",
    ">",
    "!sym",
    # Typical Kconfig-like lines
    "config FOO",
    "bool \"Enable Foo\"",
    "tristate \"Foo as module\"",
    "depends on BAR",
    "select BAZ if QUX",
    "imply ZZZ",
    "range 1 10",
    "default y",
    "help",
    # Misc
    "WARNING:",
    "error code",
    "title",
]

def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=32) -> str:
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    rest_len = rng.randint(min_len - 1, max_len - 1)
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_") for _ in range(rest_len))
    return first + rest

def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with a few multi-byte code points.
    parts: List[str] = []
    while len(''.join(parts)) < max_len:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.7:
            parts.append(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-:/."))
        else:
            # pick from some ranges
            cp_choices = [
                rng.randint(0x00A1, 0x024F),  # Latin-1 supplement/extended
                rng.randint(0x0391, 0x03C9),  # Greek
                rng.randint(0x0400, 0x04FF),  # Cyrillic
                rng.randint(0x3040, 0x30FF),  # Japanese Hiragana/Katakana
                rng.randint(0x4E00, 0x9FFF),  # CJK Unified Ideographs
            ]
            cp = rng.choice(cp_choices)
            parts.append(chr(cp))
    s = ''.join(parts)
    return s[:max_len]

def _kconfig_snippet(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    name = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 16).upper()
    dep1 = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 16).upper()
    dep2 = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 16).upper()
    prompt = "Enable " + name
    lines = [
        f"config {name}",
        rng.choice(["bool", "tristate"]) + f" \"{prompt}\"",
        f"depends on {dep1} {rng.choice(['&&','||'])} {dep2}",
        f"default {rng.choice(['y','m','n'])}",
        f"help",
        f"  {name} detailed help text.",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines)

def _filename_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    exts = [".conf", ".cfg", ".Kconfig", ".txt", "", ".dtsi"]
    dirs = [
        "",
        "arch/x86/",
        "arch/arm/",
        "drivers/net/",
        "drivers/gpu/",
        "kernel/",
        "scripts/",
        "include/config/",
    ]
    files = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        fn = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 12)
        files.append(rng.choice(dirs) + fn + rng.choice(exts))
    # Ensure some canonical names
    files += ["Kconfig", "Makefile", "defconfig", "/tmp/test.Kconfig"]
    return files

def _build_string_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    result: List[bytes] = []
    # Start with defaults
    for s in _DEF_STRINGS:
        result.append(s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")
    # Add randomized identifiers and prompts
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 15)):
        s = _rand_ident(rng, 1, rng.randint(4, 24))
        result.append(s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        s = "Enable " + _rand_ident(rng, 3, 16)
        result.append(s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")
    # Add UTF-8 strings
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        s = _rand_utf8(rng, rng.randint(4, 32))
        result.append(s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00")
    # Add Kconfig-like snippets
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        s = _kconfig_snippet(rng)
        result.append(s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")
    # Add filenames
    for fn in _filename_pool(rng):
        result.append(fn.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")
    return result

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    chunks = []

    # Header marker to help some fuzzers detect structure (not required; still valid bytes)
    chunks.append(b"STRPOOL\x00")

    # Build a pool of null-terminated strings
    pool = _build_string_pool(rng)
    rng.shuffle(pool)

    total = sum(len(c) for c in chunks)
    for entry in pool:
        if total + len(entry) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        chunks.append(entry)
        total += len(entry)

    # Ensure at least one longer paragraph for str_append/str_printf
    if total < MAX_TOTAL - 128:
        para = (
            "This is a long help paragraph intended to exercise wrapping in gstr. "
            "It contains multiple sentences, numbers 12345, symbols == && ||, and UTF-8 like café."
        ).encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"
        if total + len(para) <= MAX_TOTAL:
            chunks.append(para)
            total += len(para)

    # Final buffer
    buf = b"".join(chunks)
    return buf

import random
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs for the xfwrite fuzzer stub.
# Fuzzer uses:
#  - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(): expects a filename to open for writing
#  - FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): provides the data buffer written via xfwrite
# Our generator only supplies the initial bytes buffer consumed by the harness
# to initialize those FUZZ_PARAM_* providers. The harness will likely split the
# buffer into filename and data regions. Since the exact harness protocol isn't
# provided, we produce a self-describing package with two sections:
#  [u32 magic]\n[u16 filename_len]\n[filename bytes]\n[u16 data_len]\n[data bytes]
#
# Conventions:
#  - magic: 0xBEEFCAFE to help harness detect our format if it supports it.
#  - filename: ASCII path with safe characters; include directory components.
#  - data: arbitrary binary blob (1..4096) with diverse content to exercise fwrite.
#
# Lengths are kept within the 4096 bytes total constraint.

SAFE_NAME_CHARS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-_."
DIR_SEPS = ["/", "/./", "/../"]

def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a plausible writable path. Many fuzzers map the provided filename
    # into a sandbox; avoid absolute paths. Include subdirs and extensions.
    # Ensure length is reasonable (<= 128 bytes).
    parts: List[str] = []
    depth = rng.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        n = rng.randint(1, 10)
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
        parts.append(s)
        # Occasionally insert a dotfile or dot segment
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            parts.append('.' if rng.random() < 0.5 else '..')
    base_len = rng.randint(3, 12)
    base = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(base_len))
    # Pick an extension commonly used in configs/binaries
    exts = [".bin", ".dat", ".cfg", ".txt", ".out", ".kcnf"]
    ext = rng.choice(exts) if rng.random() < 0.9 else ''
    path = 'tmp'  # relative sandbox-friendly prefix
    # Optionally add a random dir separator variant
    for p in parts:
        sep = rng.choice(DIR_SEPS) if rng.random() < 0.2 else '/'
        path += sep + p
    path += '/' + base + ext
    # Sanitize accidental double slashes except intentional sequences
    while '//' in path:
        path = path.replace('//', '/')
    # Ensure it's not empty and not ending with '/'
    if not path or path.endswith('/'):
        path += 'f'
    # Bound the length
    b = path.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')[:128]
    if len(b) == 0:
        b = b"f.dat"
    return b

def _rand_data(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Compose data with structured segments to exercise fwrite with varying len/count
    # while remaining valid arbitrary binary.
    # Mix of ASCII text, zeroes, high-bytes, and repeated patterns.
    target = rng.randint(1, min(1024, max_len))
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Text segment
    if target > 16 and rng.random() < 0.9:
        words = [
            b"CONFIG_FOO=y\n", b"CONFIG_BAR=m\n", b"# Kconfig snippet\n",
            b"menu \"Main\"\n", b"config BAZ\n\tbool\n",
        ]
        chunks.append(rng.choice(words))

    # Binary patterns
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        rep = rng.randint(4, 32)
        pat_len = rng.randint(1, 8)
        pat = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(pat_len))
        chunks.append(pat * rep)

    # Zero and 0xFF padding blocks
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        chunks.append(b"\x00" * rng.randint(3, 64))
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        chunks.append(b"\xFF" * rng.randint(3, 64))

    # Random bytes tail
    rand_tail = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randint(8, 128)))
    chunks.append(rand_tail)

    data = b"".join(chunks)
    if len(data) == 0:
        data = bytes([rng.randint(0, 255)])
    # Trim or extend to target size
    if len(data) > target:
        data = data[:target]
    else:
        # Pad with random bytes to reach target
        pad_len = target - len(data)
        if pad_len > 0:
            data += bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(pad_len))
    return data

def _le16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF))

def _le32(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF, (n >> 16) & 0xFF, (n >> 24) & 0xFF))

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build filename and data respecting total size <= 4096
    fname = _rand_filename(rng)
    # Reserve header 4 + 2 + 2 = 8 bytes
    max_data = 4096 - 8 - len(fname)
    if max_data < 1:
        fname = fname[: max(1, 4096 - 8 - 1)]
        max_data = 4096 - 8 - len(fname)
    data = _rand_data(rng, max(1, min(2048, max_data)))

    # Ensure non-empty data per fuzzer expectations
    if len(data) == 0:
        data = b"\x00"

    # Serialize
    magic = 0xBEEFCAFE
    # Length fields capped to 16-bit for compactness
    fname_b = fname[:65535]
    data_b = data[:min(4096 - 8 - len(fname_b), 65535)]

    buf = bytearray()
    buf += _le32(magic)
    buf += _le16(len(fname_b))
    buf += fname_b
    buf += _le16(len(data_b))
    buf += data_b

    return bytes(buf)

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: provide interesting valid filename/path strings for file_lookup and similar stubs.
# Constraints:
# - Return bytes <= 4096.
# - Deterministic per seed but with variety across calls.
# - No I/O; we only generate the content the fuzzer will place into a file and/or use as a filename.
# - Paths should be valid-looking and cover edge cases: absolute/relative, dot components, env-like, long names, unicode,
#   mixed separators, trailing slashes, extensions, hidden files, version suffixes, and nested directories.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"
EXTS = [
    "conf", "cfg", "kconfig", "Kconfig", "txt", "mk", "inc", "def", "list", "opt",
]
DIR_TOKENS = [
    "src", "drivers", "arch", "kernel", "lib", "fs", "net", "sound", "include",
    "Documentation", "scripts", "tools", "configs", "board", "platform",
]
SPECIAL_DIRS = [".", "..", ".git", ".config", ".kconfig", "build", "out", "release", "debug"]
PREFIXES = ["", "./", "../", "/", "//", "././", "../../", ".\\", "..\\", "C:/", "D:/", "\\\\?\\C:\\"]
SEP_OPTIONS = ["/", "/", "/", "/", "\\"]  # bias toward POSIX
SUFFIXES = ["", "/", "/", ""]  # sometimes trailing slash

UNICODE_FRAGMENTS = [
    "µ", "ß", "ñ", "Ø", "中", "文", "日本語", "한글", "😀", "・", "å", "é", "ø", "ç",
]

RESERVED_WIN = {"CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL", *(f"COM{i}" for i in range(1, 10)), *(f"LPT{i}" for i in range(1, 10))}

def _rnd(rs: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return seq[rs.randrange(len(seq))]

def rand_token(rs: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16, allow_unicode=True):
    # Generate a token that avoids path separators but may include dots and unicode.
    if allow_unicode and rs.random() < 0.25:
        base = rs.choices(SAFE_ASCII, k=rs.randint(min_len, max_len))
        # insert a unicode fragment at a random position
        frag = _rnd(rs, UNICODE_FRAGMENTS)
        pos = rs.randrange(len(base) + 1)
        base.insert(pos, frag)
        token = "".join(base)
    else:
        token = "".join(rs.choices(SAFE_ASCII + ".", k=rs.randint(min_len, max_len)))
    # avoid reserved Windows device names as entire path components
    if token.upper() in RESERVED_WIN:
        token = "_" + token
    # avoid empty and single dot/double dot unless explicitly chosen
    if token in {"", ".", ".."}:
        token = "t" + token.replace(".", "d")
    return token

def build_path(rs: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a prefix style
    prefix = _rnd(rs, PREFIXES)
    sep = _rnd(rs, SEP_OPTIONS)

    # Number of components
    n = rs.randint(1, 6)

    components: List[str] = []

    # Mix of known directory tokens, specials, and random tokens
    for i in range(n):
        choice = rs.random()
        if choice < 0.20:
            components.append(_rnd(rs, SPECIAL_DIRS))
        elif choice < 0.55:
            components.append(_rnd(rs, DIR_TOKENS))
        else:
            components.append(rand_token(rs, allow_unicode=True))

    # Possibly add a filename at the end with extension
    add_filename = rs.random() < 0.85
    if add_filename:
        base = rand_token(rs, min_len=1, max_len=24, allow_unicode=True)
        # Hidden file chance
        if rs.random() < 0.20 and not base.startswith('.'):
            base = "." + base
        # Version suffixes
        if rs.random() < 0.25:
            base += f"-{rs.randint(0, 9999)}"
        # Add common Kconfig-ish names sometimes
        if rs.random() < 0.25:
            base = _rnd(rs, ["Kconfig", "kconfig", "Config.in", "defconfig", base])
        # Extension
        if rs.random() < 0.90:
            ext = _rnd(rs, EXTS)
            # Dual extension occasionally
            if rs.random() < 0.10:
                base = f"{base}.default.{ext}"
            else:
                base = f"{base}.{ext}"
        components.append(base)

    # Join with mixed separators sometimes inside
    if rs.random() < 0.15:
        # randomly vary separators between components
        parts = []
        for i, comp in enumerate(components):
            parts.append(comp)
            if i != len(components) - 1:
                parts.append(_rnd(rs, SEP_OPTIONS))
        core = "".join(parts)
    else:
        core = sep.join(components)

    path = prefix + core

    # Normalize redundant separators lightly without removing intentional leading ones
    path = path.replace("//", "/" if not path.startswith("//") else "//")

    # Optionally append a trailing separator
    path += _rnd(rs, SUFFIXES)

    # Limit length to reasonable size; trim from middle if needed
    maxlen = rs.randint(32, 256)
    if len(path) > maxlen:
        # keep prefix and suffix
        keep = max(10, maxlen // 2)
        path = path[:keep] + "_" + path[-(maxlen - keep - 1):]

    return path

def assemble_payload(rs: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # For FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME the engine usually needs a path string. We'll return a single path.
    # Some harnesses may read multiple parameters from the same buffer; include newline-separated alternates occasionally.
    count = 1 if rs.random() < 0.8 else rs.randint(2, 5)
    paths = [build_path(rs) for _ in range(count)]

    # Occasionally include environment-like variable prefix to exercise CONFIG_prefix callers indirectly
    if rs.random() < 0.10:
        env_like = _rnd(rs, ["CONFIG_", "KCONFIG_PATH", "SRCDIR"]) + "=" + build_path(rs)
        paths.insert(0, env_like)

    data = ("\n".join(paths)).encode("utf-8", errors="surrogatepass")
    # Ensure NUL-terminated possibility for C consumers by sometimes appending NUL
    if rs.random() < 0.25:
        data += b"\x00"
    return data[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rs = random.Random(seed)
    return assemble_payload(rs)
